/LILIAN

Baltic Exchange Market Report 02 September 2026
Baltic Dry Index: 3331 (174)
Baltic Capesize Index: 5642 (421)
Baltic Panamax Index: 2429 (69)
Baltic Supramax Index: 1657 (7)
Baltic Handysize Index: 887 (2)
CAPESIZE
The market enjoyed a strong day, with both basins pushing higher, although the Atlantic once again led the advance. The BCI 182 5TC jumped $3,819 to $51,169, marking a new year-to-date high. In the Pacific, sentiment remained positive with an uptick in activity, while the C5 index increased $1.165 to $16.505. Three C5 miners were active, with offers initially reported in the low $16s before owners pulled back. By the afternoon, $16.00–$16.25 was heard fixed by a couple of miners, followed by reports of a third paying $16.60. The Atlantic was particularly firm, with increased activity from both South Brazil and West Africa. Following a busy afternoon yesterday, when some 8–10 fixtures were reported in the upper $38s to $39 range, the C3 index strengthened $1.773 to $42.273. The market was said to have opened with bids in the low $39s against offers above $40, with $40.00 reported fixed and talk of $40.90 circulating, although this remained unconfirmed. North Atlantic activity was also notably stronger, particularly on fronthaul business, pushing the C9 index up $7,000 to $89,167, while C8 increased $4,125 to $54,719.
PANAMAX
The Atlantic market recorded another consecutive day of gains across both the fronthaul and trans-Atlantic trades, with market participants reporting an improvement in activity levels. Tonnage availability in the North Atlantic remains evident, however, sources note that despite the recent strengthening in rates, a significant number of Owners continue to favour trans-Atlantic employment over trips to the Far East. Market participants have stated this preference could begin to place a ceiling on P1A rate growth, while simultaneously supporting stronger fronthaul bids as Charterers seek to incentivise owners to consider Far East employment. The Arriba (82,039 2019) open Taichung 3/5 September was said to have fixed for a trip with grains basis delivery Singapore via EC South America option NC South America to the Far East or SE Asia at $23,400. The Sakizaya Elegance (81,938 2015) open Singapore 20 August fixed for a trip with grains via EC South America with redelivery Singapore-Japan range at $22,000, although the Charterer remained unknown. In the Pacific, sentiment remains positive, supported by a stronger near-term export outlook from both Indonesia and Australia. In addition, there has been further discussion of Capesize stem splits, which are contributing additional demand to the market and providing further rate support for owners. The P5TC improved by a further $628 to conclude at $21,865.
SUPRAMAX
As we pass the mid week point the US Gulf was again the main driver, with the 11TC average up $91 to $20,949, however the fronthaul alone saw a significant jump of $709. Elsewhere movement was much more muted, although there definitely seemed to be more activity in all areas.

Atlantic
The MSXT Artemis (63,539 2019) prompt Abidjan went on subjects for a trip via Santos with agriprods to China at $26,000 with Reachy and there was a rumour of a 63,000-dwt fixed from US Gulf to East Mediterranean with petcoke at $33,000, although no further details emerged.

Asia
The AE Uranus (53,383 2008) Jakarta 5-9 September was reported fixed for a trip via Indonesia to China at $15,500 with Naval Bulk, however a source later heard the business may have failed, and the Medi Luna (63,371 2020) prompt in West coast India was on subjects basis delivery Port Elizabeth for a trip Singapore-Japan at $25,000 plus $250,000 ballast bonus with Cargill. The Katerina K (63,878 2017) Sohar 3-5 September fixed via Dibba to West coast India at around $26,000 and the Star New London (63,140 2015) Fujairah 1-3 September fixed a trip via Oman to South East Asia at around $20,000, but in both cases the Charterer was not mentioned.
HANDYSIZE
It was generally a mixed day of activity, with only minor fluctuations observed across both basins. The BHSI edged up by 2 points to 887, while the 7TC average rose by $41 to $15,974. In the Continent and Mediterranean, activity remained subdued and sentiment largely positional, with rates holding in line with previous fixtures. Despite limited reported fixtures, the US Gulf and South Atlantic began to see some fresh demand and increased activity, with rates reflecting a slightly firmer tone. Across Asia, the market remained positive, supported by a healthy balance between tonnage and cargo in key loading regions. The Bootes (40,093 2024) open Singapore was reported fixed for multiple legs in the $19,000's to WBC, while the An Hai Vincent (30,634 2007) open Polloc fixed via Japan to Oman with slag at around $18,000, although further details were not disclosed. The Southgate (38,016 2018) open Phu My fixed via Australia to Southeast Asia with alumina at around $17,000's. The Ocean Spring (33,633 2010) open Jakarta fixed via Australia to the Far East with grains in the mid-$15,000s, while the True Mariner (38,239 2011) open Kandla fixed to West Africa with bagged rice at around $13,000, although further details were lacking. The Devbulk Saliha (31,018 2011) open Mombasa fixed via Richards Bay to the Continent in the mid/low $13,000's, again with further details lacking. The period market was also active, with the Frida Bulker (40,161 2023) open Zhoushan reported fixed for one year in the low $17,000's by Damico, although further details were not disclosed.
